hazard_consequence_node.label: HazardConsequence
hazard_consequence_node.name: Dust explosion
hazard_consequence_node.evidence: The case study examines the "explosion and flash fires" at US Ink. The report states that "the ignition led to a dust explosion within the dust collector" and that this pressure rise then "triggered an initial flash fire" and the later larger flash fire/fireball. Witness observations were also described as "consistent with the sights and sounds of a combustible dust deflagration."
hazard_consequence_node.explanation: The main accident mechanism analyzed is spontaneous ignition of combustible dust/sludge in the ductwork, propagation to the dust collector, a dust explosion with suppression-system activation, and then back-propagation that produced the secondary flash-fire sequence. The flash fire caused the injuries, but the dust explosion is the central hazardous phenomenon and primary focus of the technical analysis.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: Gilsonite, carbon black, and clay dust mixture
entity_nodes.evidence: powdery mixture of accumulated carbon black, Gilsonite, and clay in the ductwork of the dust collection system
entity_nodes.explanation: This combustible dust mixture was the principal fuel involved in the duct and dust collector deflagration sequence.

entity_nodes.label: Material
entity_nodes.name: Hydrocarbon oil, clay, and carbon black sludge
entity_nodes.evidence: the duct sludge was a mixture of hydrocarbon oil, clay, and carbon black
entity_nodes.explanation: The accumulated sludge-like residue in the ductwork was identified as the material that self-heated and probably ignited first.

entity_nodes.label: Location
entity_nodes.name: Dust collector
entity_nodes.evidence: the ignition led to a dust explosion within the dust collector
entity_nodes.explanation: The dust explosion occurred in the dust collector, where the suppression system activated and flame propagation then moved back toward the process area.

condition_nodes.label: Phase
condition_nodes.name: Solid
condition_nodes.evidence: powdery mixture of accumulated carbon black, Gilsonite, and clay
condition_nodes.explanation: The hazardous fuel was primarily present as combustible dust/solid particulate in the ductwork and collector.

condition_nodes.label: Temperature
condition_nodes.name: High temperature
condition_nodes.evidence: the typical 240°F temperature for the mixing tanks and the maximum 300°F recorded for T-306 and T-106
condition_nodes.explanation: Heated process conditions and self-heating of residues supported the ignition scenario.

condition_nodes.label: Combustibility
condition_nodes.name: Combustible
condition_nodes.evidence: consistent with the sights and sounds of a combustible dust deflagration
condition_nodes.explanation: The involved dust/residue was capable of burning rapidly and exploding when dispersed and ignited.

condition_nodes.label: ReleaseType
condition_nodes.name: Continuous release
condition_nodes.evidence: with the system continuing to draw condensable vapors into the duct
condition_nodes.explanation: Material entered and accumulated in the ductwork over several hours of continued system operation rather than from a single sudden discharge.

condition_nodes.label: Confinement
condition_nodes.name: High confinement
condition_nodes.explanation: The deflagration occurred inside enclosed process equipment and ducting, which provided strong confinement for pressure development.

event_nodes.label: InitiatingEvent
event_nodes.name: Continuous operation of heated mixing tanks and dust collection system after commissioning
event_nodes.evidence: The CSB concluded that the explosion and flash fires occurred because of continuous manually controlled heating of the mixing tanks and operation of the dust collection system for several hours after commissioning, with the system continuing to draw condensable vapors into the duct.
event_nodes.explanation: This was the earliest abnormal operating condition that initiated the accumulation and heating of combustible residues in the ductwork.

event_nodes.label: MechanicalFailure
event_nodes.name: Dust collection system automatic shutdown malfunction
event_nodes.evidence: the dust collection system actually continued to run overnight, even when all the ink mixers were shut off
event_nodes.explanation: The new dust collection system failed to shut down as intended, allowing prolonged operation that contributed to residue accumulation and self-heating.

event_nodes.label: IgnitionSource
event_nodes.name: Spontaneous self-ignition of accumulated sludge in ductwork
event_nodes.evidence: the incident probably started with the self-heating and spontaneous ignition of the accumulated sludge (mostly Gilsonite and carbon black mixed with hydrocarbon oils) in the ductwork of the dust collection system
event_nodes.explanation: Self-heated combustible sludge/residue in the ductwork provided the ignition that initiated the explosion and flash-fire sequence.
